items.title: Eigenspaces of the diagonal operator
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a complete orthonormal family of $H$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]), let $(\lambda_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\subseteq\mathbb R$, and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]:
$$D(A)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\sum_n\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Ax=\sum_n\lambda_n\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n .$$
Then:

(a) for every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ the eigenspace of $A$ at $\lambda$ is the closed linear span of the basis vectors carrying the eigenvalue $\lambda$:
$$\ker(A-\lambda I)=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{e_n:\lambda_n=\lambda\};$$
in particular $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$ exactly when $\lambda=\lambda_n$ for some $n$;

(b) if $\lambda_m\ne\lambda_n$ whenever $m\ne n$, then $\ker(A-\lambda_nI)=\mathbb Ce_n$ for every $n$: every eigenspace is one-dimensional with eigenvector $e_n$, the eigenspaces are pairwise orthogonal, and every nonzero eigenvector of $A$ is a nonzero multiple of some $e_n$;

(c) in the situation of (b) the linear span of all eigenspaces of $A$ is $\operatorname{span}\{e_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, which is dense in $H$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** a complex Hilbert space $H$; a complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of $H$; real numbers $\lambda_n$; the diagonal operator $A$ displayed in the Statement; a real number $\lambda$.

[F1] $D(A)$ and $A$ are as displayed, $A$ is self-adjoint, $Ae_n=\lambda_ne_n$ for every $n$, and the algebraic span $D_0=\operatorname{span}\{e_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ is a core for $A$ ([[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] clauses (b), (d), (e)).

[F2] $\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}$; a series $\sum_na_ne_n$ converges in $H$ exactly when $\sum_n|a_n|^2<\infty$, and then $\bigl\|\sum_na_ne_n\bigr\|^2=\sum_n|a_n|^2$; every $x\in H$ satisfies $x=\sum_n\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n$ and $\sum_n|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2=\|x\|^2$; and the coefficients of a convergent expansion in the family are unique ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]).

## Proof

**Given:** the Hilbert space $H$, the complete orthonormal family $(e_n)$, the real numbers $\lambda_n$, the diagonal operator $A$ of [F1], and a real number $\lambda$.

1.1 [One inclusion] Let $x\in D(A)$ with coefficients $c_n=\langle x,e_n\rangle$ satisfy $Ax=\lambda x$. By [F1] both series $\sum_n\lambda_nc_ne_n$ and $\sum_n\lambda c_ne_n$ converge, so their difference $\sum_n(\lambda_n-\lambda)c_ne_n=0$ converges; its coefficients in the orthonormal family are $(\lambda_n-\lambda)c_n$, and by the uniqueness of coefficients in [F2] all of them vanish. Hence $c_n=0$ whenever $\lambda_n\ne\lambda$, so $x=\sum_{n:\lambda_n=\lambda}c_ne_n$ lies in the closed linear span of $\{e_n:\lambda_n=\lambda\}$. [given, F1, F2]

1.2 [The converse inclusion] Conversely let $I:=\{n:\lambda_n=\lambda\}$ and let $x=\sum_{n\in I}c_ne_n$ be an element of the closed linear span of $\{e_n:n\in I\}$, so that $\sum_{n\in I}|c_n|^2<\infty$ and the series converges by [F2]. Then $\sum_n\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2=\sum_{n\in I}\lambda^2|c_n|^2<\infty$, so $x\in D(A)$ by [F1], and $Ax=\sum_{n\in I}\lambda c_ne_n=\lambda x$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (a)] Steps 1.1 and 1.2 give $\ker(A-\lambda I)=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{e_n:\lambda_n=\lambda\}$ for every real $\lambda$, and this span is nonzero exactly when $\lambda\in\{\lambda_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ because $e_n\ne0$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, given]

3.1 [Clause (b)] Assume the $\lambda_n$ are pairwise distinct and let $\lambda=\lambda_k$. Then $\{n:\lambda_n=\lambda\}=\{k\}$, so step 2.1 gives $\ker(A-\lambda_kI)=\mathbb Ce_k$; every such eigenspace is one-dimensional with eigenvector $e_k\ne0$, and distinct eigenspaces are orthogonal because $\langle e_m,e_k\rangle=0$ for $m\ne k$ by [F2]. If $x\ne0$ satisfies $Ax=\lambda x$, then $\lambda=\lambda_k$ for some $k$ by step 2.1 and $x\in\mathbb Ce_k$; conversely every nonzero multiple of $e_k$ is an eigenvector by [F1]. [step 2.1, F1, F2]

4.1 [Clause (c)] The span of the union of the eigenspaces contains every $e_n$, hence contains $D_0=\operatorname{span}\{e_n\}$, which is dense in $H$ by [F1]; therefore the span of the eigenspaces is dense. [step 3.1, F1] ∎

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §2.4 pp. 73-74 (eigenvalues, eigenspaces and the multiplication-operator example)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', §1 pp. 1-9 (non-degeneracy of the oscillator ground state and the ladder spectrum)

items.title: Transport of spectral projection-valued measures along isometric bijections
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]) and let $U:H\to K$ be a bijective linear map with
$$\langle Ux,Uy\rangle_K=\langle x,y\rangle_H\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in H .$$
Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_T$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and define
$$D(T'):=U D(T),\qquad T'(Ux):=U(Tx)\quad(x\in D(T)).$$
Then:

(a) $T'$ is well defined, linear, densely defined and self-adjoint on $K$;

(b) the assignment $E(B):=U E_T(B) U^{-1}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, and it is the spectral projection-valued measure of $T'$;

(c) for every unit vector $x\in H$ the scalar laws of the two operators agree,
$$\mu^{T'}_{Ux}(B):=\|E(B)Ux\|_K^2=\|E_T(B)x\|_H^2=:\mu^{T}_x(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel});$$

(d) $\sigma(T')=\sigma(T)$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** complex Hilbert spaces $H,K$; a bijective linear isometry $U:H\to K$; a self-adjoint operator $T$ on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_T$; the operator $T'$ defined in the Statement; a real number $\lambda$ and Borel sets $B,B_n\subseteq\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Spectral theorem.** $E_T$ is the unique regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ with
$$D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{T,x}(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_T(\lambda)x\ \ (x\in D(T)),$$
where $E_{T,x}(B)=\langle E_T(B)x,x\rangle$; conversely, if a regular projection-valued measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$ satisfies the two displayed identities for an operator $S$ in place of $T$, then $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $S$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]).

[F2] **Projection-valued measures and their scalar measures.** $E_T(B)$ is an orthogonal projection for every Borel $B$, $E_T(\varnothing)=0$, $E_T(\mathbb R)=I$, $E_T(B\cap C)=E_T(B)E_T(C)$, and for pairwise disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$ one has $E_T(B)x=\sum_nE_T(B_n)x$ in norm for every $x$; the scalar pairing $E_{T,x,y}(B):=\langle E_T(B)x,y\rangle$ is a finite complex measure and $E_{T,x}(B):=E_{T,x,x}(B)=\|E_T(B)x\|^2\ge0$; the regularity of $E_T$ means that every $E_{T,x}$ is a regular Borel measure ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]).

[F3] **Spectrum as support.** For the self-adjoint operator $T$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_T$ one has $E_T(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(T))=0$ and $E_T(V)\ne0$ for every nonempty relatively open $V\subseteq\sigma(T)$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)).

[F4] **The adjoint.** For a densely defined operator $S$ on $H$, a vector $y\in H$ lies in $D(S^*)$ exactly when $x\mapsto\langle Sx,y\rangle$ is bounded on $(D(S),\|\cdot\|)$; then $S^*y$ is the unique $w\in H$ with $\langle Sx,y\rangle=\langle x,w\rangle$ for every $x\in D(S)$; and $S$ is self-adjoint exactly when $S=S^*$, that is $D(S)=D(S^*)$ and the two actions agree ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

[F5] **Inner-product calculus.** The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, $\|u\|^2=\langle u,u\rangle$, and $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\,\|v\|$ ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]).

## Proof

**Given:** the data of the Statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [The inverse is a linear isometry] Since $U$ is bijective, $U^{-1}$ exists; it is linear because $U$ is linear. For $a=Ux$ and $b=Uy$ in $K$, $\langle U^{-1}a,U^{-1}b\rangle_H=\langle x,y\rangle_H=\langle Ux,Uy\rangle_K=\langle a,b\rangle_K$; hence $U^{-1}$ is isometric, and so is $U$, so $\|Ux\|_K=\|x\|_H$ for every $x\in H$. [given, F5]

2.1 [$E$ is a projection-valued measure] For a Borel set $B$ define $E(B):=UE_T(B)U^{-1}\in\mathcal B(K)$. It is an orthogonal projection: $E(B)^2=UE_T(B)U^{-1}UE_T(B)U^{-1}=E(B)$ and $\langle E(B)a,b\rangle_K=\langle E_T(B)U^{-1}a,U^{-1}b\rangle_H=\langle U^{-1}a,E_T(B)U^{-1}b\rangle_H=\langle a,E(B)b\rangle_K$ for all $a,b\in K$, using the isometry of $U^{-1}$ and the self-adjointness of $E_T(B)$. Moreover $E(\varnothing)=0$, $E(\mathbb R)=I$, $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$, and for pairwise disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $\bigl\|E(B)a-\sum_{n\le N}E(B_n)a\bigr\|_K=\bigl\|E_T(B)U^{-1}a-\sum_{n\le N}E_T(B_n)U^{-1}a\bigr\|_H\to0$ by [F2]. Hence $E$ is a projection-valued measure on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$. [given, step 1.1, F2]

2.2 [$T'$ is well defined, linear and symmetric] If $Ux=Ux'$ then $x=x'$ by injectivity, so $T'(Ux):=U(Tx)$ is well defined; $D(T')=U D(T)$ is a linear subspace, dense because $D(T)$ is dense and $U$ is bijective, and $T'$ is linear because $T$ and $U$ are. For $x,y\in D(T)$, using the isometry of $U$ in both directions and the self-adjointness of $T$, $\langle T'Ux,Uy\rangle_K=\langle UTx,Uy\rangle_K=\langle Tx,y\rangle_H=\langle x,Ty\rangle_H=\langle Ux,UTy\rangle_K=\langle Ux,T'Uy\rangle_K$. [given, step 1.1, F5]

3.1 [$E$ is regular with transported scalar measures] For $y,z\in K$ and Borel $B$, $E_{y,z}(B):=\langle E(B)y,z\rangle_K=\langle E_T(B)U^{-1}y,U^{-1}z\rangle_H=E_{T,U^{-1}y,U^{-1}z}(B)$ by the isometry of $U^{-1}$ and the definition of $E$; in particular $E_y(B)=E_{T,U^{-1}y}(B)$ with $U^{-1}y\in H$. Since $E_T$ is regular, each $E_{T,x}$ is a regular Borel measure [F2], so each scalar measure $E_y$ of $E$ is regular and $E$ is regular. [step 2.1, F2]

3.2 [$T'$ is self-adjoint] Let $y'\in D((T')^*)$, put $z:=U^{-1}y'\in H$, $w:=(T')^*y'\in K$ and $v:=U^{-1}w\in H$. For every $x\in D(T)$, $\langle Tx,z\rangle_H=\langle UTx,y'\rangle_K=\langle T'Ux,y'\rangle_K=\langle Ux,w\rangle_K=\langle x,v\rangle_H$ by the isometry of $U^{-1}$; hence the functional $x\mapsto\langle Tx,z\rangle_H$ is bounded on $(D(T),\|\cdot\|_H)$ by $\|v\|_H\|x\|_H$, so $z\in D(T^*)=D(T)$ and $Tz=v$ by [F4]. Therefore $y'=Uz\in U D(T)=D(T')$ and $(T')^*y'=w=Uv=UTz=T'y'$; thus $D((T')^*)\subseteq D(T')$, and with step 2.2 and [F4] the operator $T'$ is self-adjoint. [step 2.2, F4, F5]

4.1 [$E$ represents $T'$] Let $y\in D(T')$, that is $x:=U^{-1}y\in D(T)$. By [F1] applied to $T$ at $x$, $\int\lambda^2\,dE_{T,x}<\infty$ and $\int\lambda\,dE_T(\lambda)x=Tx$; by step 3.1 with $y=z$, $E_y=E_{T,x}$, so $\int\lambda^2\,dE_y<\infty$ and $\int\lambda\,dE_y=\int\lambda\,dE_{T,x}$. Conversely, if $\int\lambda^2\,dE_y<\infty$ for some $y\in K$, then step 3.1 gives $\int\lambda^2\,dE_{T,U^{-1}y}<\infty$, so $U^{-1}y\in D(T)$ by [F1] and $y\in U D(T)=D(T')$. Thus $D(T')=\{y\in K:\int\lambda^2\,dE_y(\lambda)<\infty\}$, the exact domain of the unbounded integral $S:=\int\lambda\,dE(\lambda)$ against the projection-valued measure $E$. For $y\in D(T')$ and every $z\in K$, $\langle Sy,z\rangle_K=\int\lambda\,dE_{y,z}(\lambda)=\int\lambda\,dE_{T,U^{-1}y,U^{-1}z}(\lambda)=\langle TU^{-1}y,U^{-1}z\rangle_H=\langle T'y,z\rangle_K$, the middle equality by [F1] applied to $T$ at $U^{-1}y\in D(T)$; since the pairings separate points of $K$, $Sy=T'y$. By the converse clause of [F1] applied to $S=T'$ and the regular projection-valued measure $E$, the measure $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $T'$. [step 3.1, F1, F5]

4.2 [Clause (c)] For $x\in H$, $E(B)Ux=UE_T(B)U^{-1}Ux=UE_T(B)x$, so $\|E(B)Ux\|_K^2=\|E_T(B)x\|_H^2$ by the isometry of $U$; for unit $x$ this is the asserted identity of scalar laws, both sides being the values at $B$ of the positive measures $E_{Ux}$ and $E_{T,x}$ of [F2]. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, F5]

5.1 [Clause (d)] By [F3] applied to $T$, $\sigma(T)$ is the support of $E_T$; by step 4.1 the measure $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $T'$, so [F3] applied to $T'$ shows that $\sigma(T')$ is the support of $E$. For every Borel $B$, $E(B)=0$ if and only if $E_T(B)=0$, because $U$ and $U^{-1}$ are bijective; hence $E$ and $E_T$ have the same null sets and the same nonempty relatively open subsets on which they fail to vanish, so their supports -- and therefore $\sigma(T')$ and $\sigma(T)$ -- coincide. [step 4.1, F3] ∎

items.title: The quadratic-potential oscillator model of the framework
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted framework assumptions.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, in the readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix real model parameters $m>0$ (mass parameter, unit $\mathrm{kg}$), $\omega>0$ (angular frequency, unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$) and the action constant $\hbar>0$ (unit $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$) of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)4, and put
$$\ell:=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{m\omega}}>0\qquad\text{(unit }\mathrm m\text{),}$$
the model's length scale.

**(b) One-dimensional realization.** The model's one-dimensional state space is the complex Hilbert space $H_1:=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ of almost-everywhere classes with inner product linear in the first argument, taken in the scalar reading $r=1$ of the component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] for $d=1$. The model's **position** and **momentum** are the operators of that lemma at $d=1$, $r=1$, namely
$$Q:=M_x,\qquad D(Q)=\{f\in H_1:xf\in L^{2}\},\qquad (Qf)(x)=xf(x),$$
$$P:=-i\hbar D_x,\qquad D(P)=\{f\in H_1:\text{the weak derivative }D_xf\text{ lies in }L^{2}\},\qquad Pf=-i\hbar D_xf,$$
which are densely defined and self-adjoint with exactly these domains; the model assigns to $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and to $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), with outcome laws read from P2.

**(c) Energy observable.** Let $g_0,P_{g},(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the Hermite data and the unitary of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b) for the parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$, and let $A$ be the diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the family $(g_n)$ and the eigenvalues $2n+1$. The model's **energy operator** is
$$H_1:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,D A D^{-1},\qquad D(H_1):=\{f\in H_1:D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$
the operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (b); its exact domain, action, spectrum and eigenbasis are those established there. The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition. On the core $D(P_{g})$ the operator $H_1$ is the self-adjoint realization of the quadratic expression: for every $f$ in the span of the eigenbasis,
$$H_1f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}f$$
pointwise, and for every $f\in D(H_1)$ the weak identity $\int (H_1f)\varphi\,dx=\int f\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\varphi''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}\varphi\bigr)dx$ holds for every $\varphi\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R)$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (c), (d)). The formal differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}$ is the model's **quadratic potential energy plus kinetic energy** reading; no identification of $D(H_1)$ with any independently defined maximal differential-operator domain, and no separate quadratic-form-domain characterization, is asserted.

**(d) Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** For the spinless reading $s=0$ of the massive-particle model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]], with state space $H_3:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dx;\mathbb C)$, position operators $Q_j$ and momentum operators $P_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) with the domains and units of that definition, the model with common frequency $\omega$ has **energy operator** $H_3$ equal to the diagonal operator $H$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c) for $d=3$, $m_j=m$, $\omega_j=\omega$, a self-adjoint operator on $H_3$ with the domain, spectrum and core displayed there. The model assigns to $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable in the reading of clause (c); its eigenbasis and the identity $H_3=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\partial_{x_j}^{2}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x_j^{2}\bigr)$ on the core are those of that theorem, and the one-dimensional realization of clauses (b) and (c) is the coordinate specialization of this one.

**(e) Physical reading and scope.** Clause (c) defines the model quantity that the page calls the energy; it is a **model assumption** that the energy of the declared isolated particle is this assigned observable, and no measured value, no laboratory identification and no derivation of $m$ or $\omega$ from any microscopic or environmental theory is asserted. The quadratic potential is an **idealization**: for a smooth scalar potential on the line with a non-degenerate local minimum at the origin and $V''(0)>0$, the leading term of the Taylor expansion about the minimum is $\frac{1}{2}V''(0)x^{2}$ and the model with $m\omega^{2}=V''(0)$ is the corresponding leading approximation, whose deviations at finite amplitude are governed by the higher derivatives and are not developed on this page (Binney §3.1, cited in the references). The model contains no damping, no external driving, no time-dependent parameters, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic term, no relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect; those are separate model assumptions belonging to their own items. The parameters $m$ and $\omega$ are model parameters of dimensions $\mu$ and $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and all displayed quantities are read in the units fixed there.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the objects used by the theorems of this page and record the readings of P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the model's terminology. They assert no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model, no joint outcome law of position and momentum and no empirical result.

## Remarks

- **Why the model is fixed through the scaling theorem.** The operator $H_1$ is not introduced as "the differential expression with some self-adjoint extension": it is the unique self-adjoint extension of the symmetric operator on the polynomial-Gaussian core that is fixed outright by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]]. The weak identity of clause (c) then records that this operator is the realization of the quadratic expression in the sense of distributions, without claiming that its domain coincides with any maximally defined differential domain.
- **The two realizations are separate adoptions.** Clause (b) declares a particle confined to a line; P5's spacetime arena is $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}$, so the one-dimensional model is an additional idealization, not a restriction of P5. Clause (d) is the isotropic three-dimensional model of P5 at $s=0$. Later items of this page state their hypotheses for one or the other realization explicitly; results about the one-dimensional realization are not transferred to the three-dimensional one or conversely, except where the multidimensional theorem supplies the identification.
- **Units.** The quantities $\ell$, $Q$, $P$, $H_1$, $H_3$, $m$, $\omega$ and $\hbar$ are read as dimensioned model quantities: $[\ell]=\ell$, $[Q]=\ell$, $[P]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$, $[H]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, $[m]=\mu$, $[\omega]=\tau^{-1}$ and $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; the energy eigenvalues $\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$ are read in joules.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §3.1 printed pages 37-41 (PDF pages 45-49): the quadratic potential as the equilibrium approximation, the Hamiltonian (3.1), the length scale (3.15) and the stationary states
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', §1 printed pages 1-9: the quantum harmonic oscillator Hamiltonian, its length scale and its spectrum

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §8.3 printed pages 178-179 (PDF pages 190-191): the oscillator as an exactly solvable self-adjoint operator and the polynomial-Gaussian eigenbasis

items.physical_scope: The one-dimensional and isotropic three-dimensional quadratic-potential (harmonic) oscillator model of a spinless massive particle of the non-relativistic framework: state space L^2(R,dx) respectively L^2(R^3,dx), position and momentum operators with declared units m and kg m s^-1, and the assigned energy observable H_osc with unit J, whose operator is the self-adjoint realization of the formal differential expression -hbar^2/(2m) d^2/dx^2 + (m omega^2/2) x^2 fixed by the oscillator scaling theorem for the declared parameters m>0, omega>0 and hbar>0. The model is an adopted idealization: it is the leading quadratic approximation near a non-degenerate equilibrium of a smooth scalar potential, it asserts no measured values, no derivation of m or omega from any microscopic theory, no damping, driving or time dependence, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic or relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect.

items.title: The energy observable of the oscillator model: spectrum, eigenbasis and outcome law
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$ and action constant $\hbar>0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $(g_n)$, $D$, $A$, $(\psi_n)$ and $H_1$ be the Hermite family, the unitary, the dimensionless diagonal operator, the scaled eigenbasis and the energy operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a) and (b), so that $\psi_n=Dg_n$ and $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is the model's one-dimensional assigned energy observable of the model definition clause (c), and let
$$N_\psi:=DND^{-1},\qquad a_\psi:=DaD^{-1},\qquad a^\dagger_\psi:=Da^\dagger D^{-1}$$
be the transported number and ladder operators of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]], with domains $U D(N)$, $U D(a)$ and $U D(a^\dagger)$. Write $E_n:=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$ and, for the three-dimensional realization of the model definition clause (d), let $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ and $(\psi_N)_{N\in\mathbb N^3}$ be its assigned energy observable and its product eigenbasis. Then:

(a) **Spectrum, eigenbasis and simplicity.** $D(H_1)=\{f\in H_1:\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}$, the family $(\psi_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family of $H_1$ and a core for $H_1$, $H_1\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$, and the spectrum and eigenspaces are
$$\sigma(H_1)=\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\},\qquad \ker(H_1-E_nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n\quad(n\in\mathbb N);$$
the ground energy is $E_0=\hbar\omega/2$ and the gap between consecutive levels is $E_{n+1}-E_n=\hbar\omega$;

(b) **Excitation reading.** $H_1=\hbar\omega\bigl(N_\psi+\tfrac12I\bigr)$ with common domain $D(H_1)=D(N_\psi)$; $N_\psi$ is self-adjoint with spectrum $\mathbb N$ and eigenbasis $(\psi_n)$; $a_\psi$ and $a^\dagger_\psi$ are closed with $a_\psi^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$, and on the eigenbasis
$$a_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad a_\psi\psi_0=0,\qquad a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1},\qquad N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n;$$
the $\psi_n$ are exactly the eigenvectors of $N_\psi$, and the outcome law of $N_\psi$ in the pure preparation of $\psi_n$ is the point mass $\delta_n$;

(c) **Energy outcome law.** For every unit $f\in H_1$ the outcome law of the assigned energy observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ in the pure preparation of $f$ is purely atomic with
$$\mu^{H_1}_f\bigl(\{E_n\}\bigr)=|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\sum_{n:\,E_n\in B}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$$
for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, and $\mu^{H_1}_f(\sigma(H_1))=1$; in particular the law has no mass outside $\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and $E_n$ is an atom of the law of $f$ exactly when $\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\ne0$;

(d) **Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** The energy observable $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ of the model definition clause (d) has spectrum $\sigma(H_3)=\{\hbar\omega(M+\tfrac32):M\in\mathbb N\}$; for every $M\in\mathbb N$ the eigenspace $\ker(H_3-\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)I)$ has the orthonormal basis $\{\psi_N:N\in\mathbb N^{3},\ n_1+n_2+n_3=M\}$ and dimension $(M+1)(M+2)/2$; the ground energy is $\tfrac32\hbar\omega$;

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model and the cited mathematics. They concern the eigenvalue list, the eigenbasis, the excitation operators and the atomic outcome law of the model's assigned energy observable; they assert no measured spectral line, no numerical value of $m$, $\omega$ or $\hbar$, no apparatus realization, no selection rule and no transition rate. The identification of a laboratory resonance or spectral line with an eigenvalue difference of this model is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not a consequence of this theorem.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the adopted postulates P1, P2, P4, P5; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]]; the Hermite data, the unitary $D$, the diagonal operator $A$, the eigenbasis $(\psi_n)$ and the energy operator $H_1$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]]; the closed ladder and number operators of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] and their transports; a unit vector $f\in H_1$; a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$; a nonnegative integer $n$ and a nonnegative integer $M$.

[F1] **The model's assigned observables.** $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is the model's assigned energy observable and $(Q,\mathrm m)$, $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ are its assigned position and momentum observables; the flow of the isolated model is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$, so $H_1$ is a self-adjoint operator with a spectral projection-valued measure $E_{H_1}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{f}(B)=\|E_A(B)f\|^{2}$ for the assigned observable $(A,u_A)$ in the pure preparation of a unit vector $f$ ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (b), (c); [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b); [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F2] **The scaling theorem.** $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ is a bijective linear isometry with $Dg_n=\psi_n$; $(\psi_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family of $H_1$; $H_1=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}DAD^{-1}$ is self-adjoint with
$$D(H_1)=\Bigl\{f:\sum_n\hbar^{2}\omega^{2}(n+\tfrac12)^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad H_1f=\sum_n\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n,$$
spectrum $\sigma(H_1)=\{\hbar\omega(n+\frac12):n\in\mathbb N\}$, ground energy $\hbar\omega/2$, core the span of $(\psi_n)$ and pointwise differential identity $H_1F=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}F''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}F$ for $F$ in that span ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F3] **The closed ladder operators.** For the complete orthonormal family $(g_n)$ with coefficients $c_n=\langle x,g_n\rangle$ one has $D(a)=\{x:\sum_nn|c_n|^{2}<\infty\}$, $D(a^\dagger)=\{x:\sum_n(n+1)|c_n|^{2}<\infty\}$, $D(N)=\{x:\sum_nn^{2}|c_n|^{2}<\infty\}$, $a$ and $a^\dagger$ are closed with $a^{*}=a^\dagger$ and $(a^\dagger)^{*}=a$, $D(aa^\dagger)=D(a^\dagger a)=D(N)$, $a^\dagger a=N$ and $aa^\dagger=N+I$ on $D(N)$, $N$ is self-adjoint with $Ng_n=ng_n$ and spectrum $\mathbb N$, and $ag_n=\sqrt n\,g_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$, $ag_0=0$, $a^\dagger g_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,g_{n+1}$, $a^\dagger ag_n=ng_n$ ([[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] clauses (a), (b), (d), (e)).

[F4] **Eigenspaces of a diagonal operator.** For a complete orthonormal family $(e_n)$ and pairwise distinct real eigenvalues $\lambda_n$, the diagonal operator with this data and domain $\{x:\sum_n\lambda_n^{2}|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}$ has $\ker(A-\lambda_nI)=\mathbb Ce_n$ for every $n$ ([[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-eigenspaces]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F5] **Atoms and support of a spectral law.** For a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$: $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda I)$, so for a unit vector $f$ the law satisfies $\mu^{A}_f(\{\lambda\})=\|E_A(\{\lambda\})f\|^{2}$; and $\mu^{A}_f(B)=\mu^{A}_f(B\cap\sigma(A))$ with $\mu^{A}_f(\sigma(A))=1$ for every Borel $B$, while the scalar law of a pure preparation is a probability measure and is countably additive ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a), (b); [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b); [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] clause (a)).

[F6] **The multidimensional theorem.** For the three-dimensional isotropic realization the energy operator $H_3$ of the model definition clause (d) is self-adjoint with the domain and core displayed in [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c), and its spectrum is $\{\hbar\omega(M+\frac32):M\in\mathbb N\}$ with the eigenvalue $\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)$ having multiplicity $\binom{M+2}{2}=(M+1)(M+2)/2$ and eigenspace spanned by the orthonormal family $\{\psi_N:\sum_jn_j=M\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clauses (c), (d)).

[F7] **Transport along isometric bijections.** For complex Hilbert spaces $H,K$, a bijective linear isometry $U:H\to K$ and a self-adjoint $T$ on $H$, the operator $UTU^{-1}$ with domain $U D(T)$ is self-adjoint, has the same spectrum as $T$, and satisfies $\mu^{UTU^{-1}}_{Ux}(B)=\mu^{T}_x(B)$ for every unit $x\in H$ and Borel $B$ ([[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a), (c), (d)).

## Proof

**Given:** the data of the Statement together with [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [The diagonal form of $H_1$] By [F2], $(\psi_n)$ is complete orthonormal, $H_1$ has domain $\{f:\sum_nE_n^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}$ and acts by $H_1f=\sum_nE_n\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n$; since $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$ satisfies $n^{2}\le4(n+\frac12)^{2}$ and $(n+\frac12)^{2}\le2n^{2}+\frac12$ for every $n\in\mathbb N$, the domain condition is equivalent to $\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty$, and the family and the real numbers $E_n$ are pairwise distinct nonnegative numbers with $E_0=\hbar\omega/2$ and $E_{n+1}-E_n=\hbar\omega$. Thus $H_1$ is the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [F4] for the family $(\psi_n)$ and the eigenvalues $E_n$, and the span of $(\psi_n)$ is a core. [given, F2, F4, algebra]

1.2 [Transported ladder and number operators] The map $D$ is a bijective linear isometry by [F2], and the operators $N_\psi=DND^{-1}$, $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$, $a^\dagger_\psi=Da^\dagger D^{-1}$ have the transported domains $D(N_\psi)=D\,D(N)$, $D(a_\psi)=D\,D(a)$, $D(a^\dagger_\psi)=D\,D(a^\dagger)$; because $\psi_n=Dg_n$ and $D$ preserves the inner product, the coefficients satisfy $\langle Dx,\psi_n\rangle=\langle x,g_n\rangle$, so by [F3] $D(N_\psi)=\{f:\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}$ and the identities of [F3] transport: $D(a_\psi a^\dagger_\psi)=D(a^\dagger_\psi a_\psi)=D(N_\psi)$, on which $a^\dagger_\psi a_\psi=N_\psi$ and $a_\psi a^\dagger_\psi=N_\psi+I$, and $N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n$, $a_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}$ ($n\ge1$) with $a_\psi\psi_0=0$, $a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}$. For the non-self-adjoint pair, closedness and the adjoint relations transport by the direct pairing computation: for $x\in D(a_\psi)$ and $y\in D(a^\dagger_\psi)$, $\langle a_\psi x,y\rangle=\langle aD^{-1}x,D^{-1}y\rangle=\langle D^{-1}x,a^\dagger D^{-1}y\rangle=\langle x,a^\dagger_\psi y\rangle$, so $a_\psi\subseteq(a^\dagger_\psi)^{*}$ and $a^\dagger_\psi\subseteq a_\psi^{*}$; and if $x_k\to x$ with $a_\psi x_k\to y$, then $D^{-1}x_k\to D^{-1}x$ and $aD^{-1}x_k=D^{-1}a_\psi x_k\to D^{-1}y$, so closedness of $a$ gives $D^{-1}x\in D(a)$ and $aD^{-1}x=D^{-1}y$, that is $x\in D(a_\psi)$ and $a_\psi x=y$: $a_\psi$ is closed, and the same argument with $a^\dagger$ makes $a^\dagger_\psi$ closed and forces equalities in the two inclusions. By [F7] applied with $U=D$ and $T=N$, the operator $N_\psi$ is self-adjoint with $\sigma(N_\psi)=\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$ and $\mu^{N_\psi}_{Dx}(B)=\mu^{N}_x(B)$ for every unit $x$ and Borel $B$. [given, F2, F3, F7]

1.3 [The three-dimensional realization] By [F6] the spectrum of $H_3$ is $\{\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)\}=\{E^{(3)}_M:M\in\mathbb N\}$, the eigenspace at $E^{(3)}_M$ has the orthonormal basis $\{\psi_N:n_1+n_2+n_3=M\}$ and dimension $(M+1)(M+2)/2$, and the least eigenvalue is $\frac32\hbar\omega$; this is clause (d), whose self-adjointness, domain and core assertions are those of [F6]. [given, F6]

2.1 [Spectrum and eigenspaces of $H_1$] By step 1.1 the operator $H_1$ is the diagonal operator of [F4] with the pairwise distinct eigenvalues $E_n$, and by [F2] its spectrum is $\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, a closed discrete set whose least element is $E_0$ and whose consecutive gaps are $\hbar\omega$; [F4] gives $\ker(H_1-E_nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n$ for every $n$, and [F2] gives that $(\psi_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family and a core. This is clause (a). [step 1.1, F2, F4]

2.2 [Number-operator identity] By steps 1.1 and 1.2, $D(H_1)=\{f:\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}=D(N_\psi)$ and both operators act diagonally on the family, with $H_1$ having eigenvalues $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$ and $N_\psi$ having eigenvalues $n$; hence $H_1=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\frac12I)$ with common domain $D(H_1)=D(N_\psi)$. By step 1.2 and [F4] the eigenspaces of $N_\psi$ are $\ker(N_\psi-nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n$, so its eigenvectors are exactly the nonzero multiples of the $\psi_n$, and its spectrum is $\mathbb N$ by [F7]. For the preparation of the unit eigenvector $\psi_n$, [F5] and the eigenspace identity give $\mu^{N_\psi}_{\psi_n}(\{n\})=\|E_{N_\psi}(\{n\})\psi_n\|^{2}=\|\psi_n\|^{2}=1$; since the scalar law of a pure preparation is a probability measure [F5], the law is the point mass $\delta_n$. Together with the ladder actions of step 1.2 this is clause (b). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F4, F5, F7]

3.1 [Atoms of the energy law] By [F1], $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model whose outcome law in the pure preparation of a unit vector $f$ is $\mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\|E_{H_1}(B)f\|^{2}$. For every $n$, [F4] and step 2.1 give $\ker(H_1-E_nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n$, so the orthogonal projection $E_{H_1}(\{E_n\})$ is the projection onto $\mathbb C\psi_n$ by the first clause of [F5]; for a unit $f$ this gives $\mu^{H_1}_f(\{E_n\})=\|E_{H_1}(\{E_n\})f\|^{2}=|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$. [step 2.1, F1, F5]

4.1 [The full law and its support] Let $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ be Borel. By the support clause of [F5], $\mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\mu^{H_1}_f(B\cap\sigma(H_1))$ and $\mu^{H_1}_f(\sigma(H_1))=1$; by step 2.1, $\sigma(H_1)=\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, so $B\cap\sigma(H_1)$ is the countable union of the disjoint singletons $\{E_n\}$ with $E_n\in B$, and countable additivity of the probability measure $\mu^{H_1}_f$ gives $\mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\sum_{n:E_n\in B}\mu^{H_1}_f(\{E_n\})=\sum_{n:E_n\in B}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$ by step 3.1. In particular the law has no mass on Borel sets disjoint from $\{E_n\}$, and $E_n$ is an atom of the law of $f$ exactly when $\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\ne0$. This is clause (c). [step 2.1, step 3.1, F5]

5.1 [Status] Clauses (a), (b) and (c) were obtained from the postulates, the adopted model, the scaling theorem, the closed ladder operators and the general spectral law facts; clause (d) from the multidimensional theorem. No measured spectral line, no numerical value of $m$, $\omega$ or $\hbar$, no apparatus model, no selection rule and no transition rate entered, and the identification of a laboratory resonance with an eigenvalue difference is a tested identification under P7, not a consequence of the argument. This is clause (e). [step 1.3, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: The coherent states of the oscillator model
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 in the reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and length scale $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite family of $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, let $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the scaling unitary and $(\psi_n)$ the scaled eigenbasis of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b), with $\psi_n=Dg_n$; let $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$ and $N_\psi=DND^{-1}$ be the transported annihilation and number operators of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]], with the domains fixed in the model's spectrum theorem.

**(b) The family.** For $z\in\mathbb C$ let $\psi^{(y)}_z$ be the coherent vector of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clause (a),
$$\psi^{(y)}_z:=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,g_n\in L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy),$$
the series converging in $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, and define the model's **coherent state** with label $z$ by
$$\Psi_z:=D\psi^{(y)}_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,\psi_n\in H_1 .$$
The family $(\Psi_z)_{z\in\mathbb C}$ is the model's **coherent-state family**, and $z$ is its **amplitude-phase label**.

**(c) Basic properties.** The following properties of the family are those established in the cited items and are recorded here as part of the definition's reading: the series for $\Psi_z$ converges and $\|\Psi_z\|=1$, so by P1 the ray $[\Psi_z]$ is a pure preparation of the model when it is declared as one; $\Psi_z\in D(N_\psi^{k})$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$; $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$, so $\Psi_z$ is a unit eigenvector of the annihilation operator with eigenvalue $z$; $\langle\Psi_z,\Psi_w\rangle=e^{-|z-w|^{2}/2}$ for all $z,w$, so distinct labels define distinct preparations and no two members of the family are orthogonal; and $\Psi_0=\psi_0$ is the ground eigenvector of the energy operator. ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), transported by the unitary $D$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (a).)

**(d) Reading of the label.** The label $z$ is dimensionless (it is a complex number, not a quantity with a physical dimension). Its modulus and argument are read as the amplitude and phase labels of the preparation: the model's fluctuation and evolution results on this page compute the preparation means of position, momentum and excitation number, and they identify $|z|^{2}$ with the mean excitation number and show that the mean position and momentum rotate with the phase of $z$ at the angular frequency $\omega$. Clause (d) records this intended reading; the numerical content is supplied by those results, not asserted here.

**(e) Scope.** The definition declares a one-parameter family of preparations of the one-dimensional model and fixes its notation. It does not assert that the coherent states are the only preparations with time-independent position or momentum spreads, it does not assert minimality of any uncertainty product (that is a separate result for this family), it does not construct a displacement operator, an overcompleteness relation or a resolution of unity, and it makes no measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The two presentations of the family -- as eigenvectors of the annihilation operator, as in clause (b), and as translated ground states -- are not identified here; only the former is defined.

## Remarks

- **Why the label is not an observable.** The label $z$ indexes the family; it is not the outcome of a measurement of any assigned observable of the model. Statements about the distribution of $z$ would require a separate preparation model for the labels, which this definition does not introduce.
- **Not an orthonormal family.** The inner products of clause (c) show that no two distinct coherent states are orthogonal, so the family is not an orthonormal basis and its members are not the energy eigenstates. The energy eigenbasis remains $(\psi_n)$; the coherent states are superpositions with Poisson-type weights, a fact used by the fluctuation and evolution items of this page.

items.physical_scope: The coherent states of the one-dimensional quadratic-potential oscillator model of the framework: for each complex dimensionless label z the unit vector Psi_z obtained by transporting the coherent vector of the Hermite oscillator basis along the model's scaling unitary, its properties as a preparation of the model (normalization, annihilation-operator eigenvalue z, non-orthogonality), and the reading of the modulus and argument of z. The definition asserts no measurement procedure, no uniqueness or minimality property among preparations, no overcompleteness or resolution of unity, no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

items.title: Fluctuations of the oscillator coherent states and the position-momentum relation of the model
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q$ and $P$ be the model's position and momentum observables with their declared units ($\mathrm m$ and $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$), let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $\Delta_{\rho}A$ be the preparation spread of an assigned sharp observable in the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and write $\langle A\rangle_z:=\langle A\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle$ for the model's coherent preparation of label $z$. Then:

(a) **Coherent spreads.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector $\Psi_z$ lies in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation spreads of $Q$ and $P$ in the pure preparation of $\Psi_z$ exist, and
$$\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$

(b) **Position-momentum relation of the model.** Every unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ satisfies
$$\Delta_{f}Q\,\Delta_{f}P\ge\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
read in the product unit $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; consequently the value $\hbar/2$ attained in (a) is the minimum over the common domain, and it is attained by every coherent preparation;

(c) **Saturation.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$, with the centered vectors
$$x_z:=(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,\qquad y_z:=(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,$$
one has $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=-i\hbar/2$; in particular $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent, so $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$;

(d) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the cited preparation-moment and uncertainty results and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two separately assigned outcome laws of $Q$ and $P$ in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law of position and momentum, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, no dynamics and no empirical value. Whether a laboratory preparation and apparatus realize the pair of observables and produce this spread is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the adopted postulates P1, P2, P5; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the one-dimensional oscillator model with parameters $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and length $\ell$; the coherent states $\Psi_z$; a unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$; a complex number $z$.

[F1] **The model's observables.** $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ are assigned sharp observables of the model with $D(Q)=\{f:xf\in L^{2}\}$, $Qf=xf$, $D(P)=\{f:D_xf\in L^{2}\}$, $Pf=-i\hbar D_xf$, where $D_x$ is the weak derivative, and $Q,P$ are the $d=1$, $r=1$ instances of the componentwise operators of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]; the flow of the isolated model is generated by the assigned energy observable $H_1$ ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (b), (c); [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]; [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)).

[F2] **Coherent data.** For every $z$: $\Psi_z$ is a unit vector with $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$ and $\Psi_z\in D(N_\psi^{k})$ for every $k$; $\langle\Psi_z,\Psi_w\rangle=e^{-|z-w|^{2}/2}$; and $\Psi_0=\psi_0$ ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]] clauses (b), (c); [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e)).

[F3] **Exact coherent quantities.** With $Q$ and $P$ the position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ and $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$, $a^\dagger_\psi=Da^\dagger D^{-1}$ the transported ladder operators,
$$Q\Psi_z=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\bigl(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi\bigr)\Psi_z,\qquad P\Psi_z=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}\bigl(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi\bigr)\Psi_z,$$
and the quadratic-form means and variances of the coherent vectors are
$$\langle Q\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z,\qquad\langle P\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z,$$
$$\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z\|^{2}=\frac{\ell^{2}}{2},\qquad\|(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z\|^{2}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\ell^{2}};$$
and $\|a_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}$, $\|a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}+1$; also the adjoint relation $(a_\psi)^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$ holds, the transport of $a^{*}=a^\dagger$ along the unitary $D$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-evolution-and-variance]] clauses (d), (e); [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clause (e); [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] clauses (b), (d), (e)).

[F4] **Means, variances and spreads.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ and a unit vector $f\in D(A)$ the mean and second moment of the outcome law exist, $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_f=\langle Af,f\rangle$, $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_f=\|Af\|^{2}$, and the preparation variance and spread are
$$\operatorname{Var}_{f}(A)=\|(A-\langle Af,f\rangle I)f\|^{2},\qquad \Delta_{f}A=\operatorname{Var}_{f}(A)^{1/2},$$
read in the unit $u_A$ and its square ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b), (c), (d)).

[F5] **Product domain and commutator in one dimension.** For $d=1$, $r=1$ the product domain is $D(QP)\cap D(PQ)=\{f:D_xf,xf,xD_xf\in L^{2}\}$ and $(QP-PQ)\varphi=i\hbar\varphi$ for every $\varphi$ in it ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-commutator-identity]] clauses (b), (c)).

[F6] **Robertson relation.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_A)$, $(B,u_B)$ and a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$: $\Delta_{\psi}A\Delta_{\psi}B\ge|\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle|$; and if in addition $\psi\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, then $\Delta_{\psi}A\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\frac12|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle|$ ([[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F7] **Approximation by product-domain vectors.** For every nonzero $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ there is a sequence of unit vectors $\varphi_k\in D(QP)\cap D(PQ)$ with $\varphi_k\to f/\|f\|$, $Q\varphi_k\to Qf/\|f\|$, $P\varphi_k\to Pf/\|f\|$, and with $\langle Q\varphi_k,\varphi_k\rangle\to\langle Qf,f\rangle/\|f\|^{2}$, $\|Q\varphi_k\|\to\|Qf\|/\|f\|$, and the analogous momentum limits ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-approximation-by-product-domain-vectors]]).

[F8] **Inner-product calculus and Cauchy-Schwarz.** The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, $\|u\|^{2}=\langle u,u\rangle$, $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\,\|v\|$ with equality if and only if $u,v$ are linearly dependent, and inner products and norms are continuous for norm convergence ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]).

## Proof

**Given:** the data of the Statement and [F1]-[F8].

1.1 [The model's operators and the coherent formulas] By [F1] the model's $Q$, $P$ are the $d=1$, $r=1$ componentwise operators with the displayed dense domains, and both are assigned sharp observables; by [F2] each $\Psi_z$ is a unit vector with $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$, $\|a_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}$ and $\|a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}+1$. By [F3] the vectors $Q\Psi_z=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$ and $P\Psi_z=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$ lie in $H_1$, so $\Psi_z\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$, and the displayed coherent means and central norms hold. [given, F1, F2, F3]

1.2 [Spreads as centered norms] Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ be a unit vector. By [F4] applied to the assigned observables $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$, the outcome-law means and variances exist and $\Delta_{f}Q^{2}=\|(Q-\langle Qf,f\rangle I)f\|^{2}=\|Qf\|^{2}-\langle Qf,f\rangle^{2}$, and likewise $\Delta_{f}P^{2}=\|Pf\|^{2}-\langle Pf,f\rangle^{2}$. [given, F4]

1.3 [Bound on the product domain] Let $\varphi\in D(QP)\cap D(PQ)$ be a unit vector. By [F5], $(QP-PQ)\varphi=i\hbar\varphi$, so $\langle[Q,P]\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\langle i\hbar\varphi,\varphi\rangle=i\hbar\langle\varphi,\varphi\rangle=i\hbar$ by linearity of the pairing in its first argument. By the Robertson form of [F6] applied to the assigned sharp observables $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$, $\Delta_{\varphi}Q\Delta_{\varphi}P\ge\frac12|i\hbar|=\hbar/2$. [given, F5, F6]

1.4 [Approximating a common-domain vector] Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ be a unit vector. By [F7] there is a sequence of unit vectors $\varphi_k\in D(QP)\cap D(PQ)$ with $\varphi_k\to f$, $Q\varphi_k\to Qf$, $P\varphi_k\to Pf$, $\langle Q\varphi_k,\varphi_k\rangle\to\langle Qf,f\rangle$, $\|Q\varphi_k\|\to\|Qf\|$ and the analogous momentum limits. [given, F7]

2.1 [Clause (a)] By step 1.1 and step 1.2 applied to the unit vector $\Psi_z\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation variances are the central squared norms of [F3]: $\operatorname{Var}_{\Psi_z}(Q)=\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z\|^{2}=\ell^{2}/2$ and $\operatorname{Var}_{\Psi_z}(P)=\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$; taking square roots gives $\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$ and $\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$, whose product is $\hbar/2$ in the unit $\mathrm m\cdot\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F3]

2.2 [Clause (b), relation] Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ be a unit vector and let $(\varphi_k)$ be the approximating sequence of step 1.4. For every $k$, step 1.3 gives $\Delta_{\varphi_k}Q\Delta_{\varphi_k}P\ge\hbar/2$; by step 1.2, $\Delta_{\varphi_k}Q^{2}=\|Q\varphi_k\|^{2}-\langle Q\varphi_k,\varphi_k\rangle^{2}$, and the limits of step 1.4 together with the continuity of the inner product [F8] give $\Delta_{\varphi_k}Q^{2}\to\|Qf\|^{2}-\langle Qf,f\rangle^{2}=\Delta_{f}Q^{2}$, and likewise $\Delta_{\varphi_k}P^{2}\to\Delta_{f}P^{2}$. Taking square roots and passing to the limit in the inequality gives $\Delta_{f}Q\Delta_{f}P\ge\hbar/2$. [step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, F8]

3.1 [Clause (c), saturation] Fix $z$ and put $u:=(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$, $v:=(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$, both in $H_1$ by step 1.1. Using the conjugate-linearity in the second argument, the coherent data $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$ and the adjoint relation $(a_\psi)^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$ of [F2] and [F3], so that $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=z$, $\langle\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=z$ and $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z$, together with $\|\Psi_z\|=1$ and $\|a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}+1$, the four pairings are $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,a_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$, $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=z\langle\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=z^{2}$, $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,a_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z^{2}$ and $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}+1$, so $\langle u,v\rangle=|z|^{2}-z^{2}+\overline z^{2}-(|z|^{2}+1)=\overline z^{2}-z^{2}-1$; hence, using the first formula of [F3] and $\overline{\hbar/(i\ell\sqrt2)}=i\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$, $\langle Q\Psi_z,P\Psi_z\rangle=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\cdot\frac{i\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2}\langle u,v\rangle=\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\overline z^{2}-z^{2}-1\bigr)=2\hbar\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z-\frac{i\hbar}{2}$, because $\overline z^{2}-z^{2}=(z-\overline z)(\overline z+z)=-4i\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z$. By [F3], $\langle Q\rangle_z\langle P\rangle_z=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z\cdot\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z=2\hbar\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z$, so $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=\langle Q\Psi_z,P\Psi_z\rangle-\langle Q\rangle_z\langle P\rangle_z=-\frac{i\hbar}{2}$. Therefore $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$, while step 2.1 gives $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\hbar/2$, so equality holds in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality of [F8] and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F3, F8]

3.2 [Clause (b), minimality] By step 2.2 every unit vector in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$ has spread product at least $\hbar/2$, and by step 2.1 every coherent preparation attains the value $\hbar/2$; hence the minimum of the spread product over the unit vectors of the common domain is $\hbar/2$, attained by each $[\Psi_z]$. [step 2.1, step 2.2]

4.1 [Clause (d)] The spread values and the relation were obtained from the model's assigned observables, the preparation-moment theorem, the product-domain commutator, the cutoff approximation and the Robertson relation; the saturation computation used the same operators and the exact coherent-state quantities. No joint outcome law, apparatus resolution, disturbance, dynamics or empirical value entered, and the identification of a laboratory pair with $(Q,P)$ is a tested identification under P7. This is clause (d). [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

The statement is a conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2 and P5, of the adopted oscillator model, of the cited uncertainty and moment results and of the cited mathematics; it concerns the two separately assigned outcome laws in one preparation and asserts no joint outcome law, no apparatus resolution, no disturbance and no empirical result.

items.title: Evolution of the oscillator coherent states: classical mean motion and stationary fluctuations
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ be the model's flow, let $\Psi_z$ be the coherent state of label $z\in\mathbb C$, put $z(t):=ze^{-i\omega t}$ and, for $|z|>0$, $x_0:=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z$, $p_0:=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z$. Then:

(a) **Coherent evolution.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$, $U(t)$ is a bijective linear isometry of $H_1$ and
$$U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\,\Psi_{z(t)};$$
consequently the preparation $[\Psi_z]$ evolves under the model's Schroedinger dynamics to the coherent preparation $[\Psi_{z(t)}]$, and the labels of the evolved family rotate with angular frequency $\omega$;

(b) **Classical mean motion.** The preparation means of position and momentum at time $t$ are
$$\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t),\qquad \langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t),$$
equivalently, for every $t\in\mathbb R$, $x(t)=x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $p(t)=p_0\cos\omega t-m\omega x_0\sin\omega t$ with $x(t):=\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}$, $p(t):=\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}$; these functions are differentiable with $\dot x(t)=\frac{p(t)}{m}$ and $\dot p(t)=-m\omega^{2}x(t)$ for every $t$, so the means follow the classical harmonic motion of frequency $\omega$ through $(x_0,p_0)$;

(c) **Stationary fluctuations.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$ the evolved preparation has
$$\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$
the position and momentum spreads and their product are constant along the evolution;

(d) **Energy statistics.** The mean and the outcome law of the assigned energy observable in the coherent preparation are
$$\langle H_1\rangle_{z}=\hbar\omega\Bigl(|z|^{2}+\frac12\Bigr),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}\bigl(\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\}\bigr)=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
the law of a Poisson variable of parameter $|z|^{2}$ shifted by $\hbar\omega/2$; consequently $\Delta_{\Psi_z}H_1=\hbar\omega|z|$;

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the model's spectrum theorem, the coherent-state fluctuation theorem and the cited mathematics. They concern the exact evolution of the model's coherent preparations and the statistics of its assigned observables; no measurement record, no apparatus realization, no damping or driving and no empirical value is asserted, and the identification of the mean motion with the motion of a laboratory oscillator is a tested identification under P7.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the adopted postulates P1, P2, P4, P5; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the one-dimensional oscillator model with parameters $m,\omega,\hbar>0$, length $\ell$ and energy operator $H_1$; the coherent states $\Psi_z$; a complex number $z$ and a real number $t$.

[F1] **The model's flow.** $H_1$ is the model's assigned energy observable, and the model's flow is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)=\int e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_{H_1}(\lambda)$ of the autonomous-dynamics reading of the model definition, whose generator is $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_1$ with domain $D(H_1)$ ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (c); [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a), (b), (c); [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]).

[F2] **Explicit flow and coherent evolution.** The family $U(t)f=\sum_ne^{-i\omega(n+\frac12)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n$ is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_1$, so it is the flow of [F1]; and for every $z$, $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{ze^{-i\omega t}}$, while the evolved coherent means and variances are $\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t)$, $\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t)$, $\operatorname{Var}(Q)_{z(t)}=\ell^{2}/2$, $\operatorname{Var}(P)_{z(t)}=\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$ with $z(t)=ze^{-i\omega t}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-evolution-and-variance]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (e), (f); [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (c)).

[F3] **Coherent coefficients and the energy law.** $\Psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\psi_n$ with coefficients $\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}$; the energy outcome law of the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is $\mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}(B)=\sum_{n:E_n\in B}|\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$ with $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$; and $\langle H_1\rangle_z=\hbar\omega(|z|^{2}+\frac12)$ because $H_1=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\frac12I)$ and $\langle N_\psi\rangle_z=|z|^{2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (e); [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]] clause (b); [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-energy-spectrum-and-completeness]] clauses (b), (c); [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] clause (e)).

[F4] **Euler's formula, parity and derivatives.** For real $\theta$, $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$, hence $e^{-i\omega t}=\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t$ and $z(t)=(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)+i(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)$ for $z=z_1+iz_2$; the trigonometric functions satisfy $\sin'=\cos$, $\cos'=-\sin$, $\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta$ and $\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[cor-complex-trigonometric-and-hyperbolic-derivatives]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]]).

[F5] **Means and spreads.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ and a unit vector $f\in D(A)$ the mean and second moment of the outcome law exist with mean $\langle Af,f\rangle$ and variance $\|(A-\langle Af,f\rangle I)f\|^{2}$, and the preparation spread is its square root ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b), (c), (d)).

[F6] **Coherent fluctuations.** For every $w\in\mathbb C$ one has $\Delta_{\Psi_w}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$, $\Delta_{\Psi_w}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ and $\Delta_{\Psi_w}Q\Delta_{\Psi_w}P=\hbar/2$ ([[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-fluctuations]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F7] **The exponential series.** For every real $s$, $e^{s}=\sum_{n\ge0}s^{n}/n!$ as the sum of an absolutely convergent series, and $\sum_{n\ge1}n\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=se^{s}$, $\sum_{n\ge2}n(n-1)\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=s^{2}e^{s}$ by reindexing ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]).

## Proof

**Given:** the data of the Statement and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 [The flow and its coherent action] By [F1] the model's flow is the strongly continuous unitary group generated by $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_1$; by [F2] the explicit spectral family $U(t)f=\sum_ne^{-i\omega(n+\frac12)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n$ has the same generator, so by the uniqueness of the generator recorded in the autonomous-dynamics reading the two families agree, and $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ for every $z$ and $t$. [given, F1, F2]

1.2 [Energy law of the coherent preparation] By [F3] the coefficients of $\Psi_z$ in the eigenbasis are $\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}$, so $|\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ and the energy law is the atomic law $\mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}(\{E_n\})=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ with $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$; and the mean energy is $\langle H_1\rangle_z=\hbar\omega(|z|^{2}+\frac12)$ by [F3]. [given, F3]

1.3 [Euler and trigonometric calculus] By [F4], $e^{-i\omega t}=\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t$, so for $z=z_1+iz_2$ one has $z(t)=z(\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t)=(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)+i(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)$, and the derivatives of $\sin$ and $\cos$ are $\cos$ and $-\sin$. [given, F4]

2.1 [Clause (a)] By step 1.1, $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ for every $t$; since $U(t)$ is a bijective linear isometry by [F1], the Schroedinger-picture state of the preparation $[\Psi_z]$ at time $t$ is the ray $[U(t)\Psi_z]=[\Psi_{z(t)}]$, which is again a coherent preparation; the label $z(t)=ze^{-i\omega t}$ rotates with angular frequency $\omega$. [step 1.1, F1]

2.2 [Clause (b), complex form] By step 1.1 the evolved vector is $e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$, and multiplying by the phase $e^{-i\omega t/2}$ does not change the quadratic-form means; by [F2] and [F5], $\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t)$ and $\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t)$. [step 1.1, F2, F5]

2.3 [Clause (c)] By step 1.1 the preparation at time $t$ is the coherent preparation of label $z(t)$, so [F6] applied with $w=z(t)$ gives $\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$, $\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ and product $\hbar/2$ for every $t$: the spreads are constant along the evolution. [step 1.1, F6]

2.4 [Clause (d), Poisson law and energy spread] Let $p_n:=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ and $s:=|z|^{2}$. By step 1.2 the law is $\mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}(\{E_n\})=p_n$; by [F7], $\sum_np_n=e^{-s}\sum_n\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=1$, $\sum_nnp_n=e^{-s}\sum_nn\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=e^{-s}se^{s}=s$, and $\sum_nn^{2}p_n=e^{-s}\sum_nn^{2}\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=e^{-s}\bigl(s^{2}e^{s}+se^{s}\bigr)=s^{2}+s$, because $n^{2}=n(n-1)+n$ and the two reindexed series of [F7] apply. Hence the variance of the law is $\sum_n(n-s)^{2}p_n=(s^{2}+s)-s^{2}=s=|z|^{2}$, so the energy spread is $\Delta_{\Psi_z}H_1=\hbar\omega|z|$ and the law is the Poisson law of parameter $|z|^{2}$ carried by the shifted energies $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$. [step 1.2, F7]

3.1 [Clause (b), classical form] By step 2.2 and step 1.3, with $z=z_1+iz_2$, $x(t)=\sqrt2\ell(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)$ and $p(t)=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)$; since $x_0=\sqrt2\ell z_1$ and $\frac{p_0}{m\omega}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_2}{\ell m\omega}=\sqrt2\ell z_2$ by $\ell^{2}=\hbar/(m\omega)$, while $m\omega x_0=\sqrt2\,m\omega\ell z_1=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_1}{\ell}$ by the same identity, the displays $x(t)=x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $p(t)=p_0\cos\omega t-m\omega x_0\sin\omega t$ follow. Differentiating with the trigonometric derivatives of step 1.3 gives $\dot x(t)=-x_0\omega\sin\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m}\cos\omega t=\frac{p(t)}{m}$ and $\dot p(t)=-p_0\omega\sin\omega t-m\omega x_0\omega\cos\omega t=-m\omega^{2}\bigl(x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t\bigr)=-m\omega^{2}x(t)$ for every $t$. [step 1.3, step 2.2, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Clause (e)] Clauses (a), (b), (c) and (d) were obtained from the model's flow and energy observable, the explicit coherent evolution, the coherent fluctuation theorem and the exponential and trigonometric identities; no measurement record, apparatus model, damping or driving and no empirical value entered, and the identification of the mean motion with a laboratory oscillator is a tested identification under P7. This is clause (e). [step 2.1, step 2.3, step 2.4, step 3.1] ∎

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the oscillator page
items.statement:
## What the page adopts and proves

**Adopted.** The page adopts the framework postulates P1, P2 and P4 and the massive-particle postulates P5 in the readings fixed by the framework pages, and it adopts the quadratic-potential oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] as a model assumption: a declared spinless particle, a one-dimensional realization with state space $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$, an isotropic three-dimensional realization with state space $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dx)$, model parameters $m>0$ (kg), $\omega>0$ ($\mathrm s^{-1}$) and action constant $\hbar>0$ ($\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$), and the assigned energy observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ respectively $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ fixed through the oscillator scaling and multidimensional theorems. The coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]] is a further declared one-parameter family of preparations of the one-dimensional realization.

**Proved.** [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-energy-spectrum-and-completeness]] gives the exact eigenvalue list $\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$, the one-dimensional eigenspaces $\mathbb C\psi_n$, completeness of the Hermite eigenbasis, the excitation operators and the atomic energy outcome law, and the isotropic three-dimensional spectrum $\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)$ with multiplicities $(M+1)(M+2)/2$; [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-fluctuations]] computes the coherent position and momentum spreads $\ell/\sqrt2$ and $\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$, proves the model's position-momentum relation $\Delta Q\Delta P\ge\hbar/2$ on the common domain and the saturation of the bound in every coherent preparation; and [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-evolution]] proves that the flow carries the coherent preparation $[\Psi_z]$ to $[\Psi_{ze^{-i\omega t}}]$, that the preparation means perform the classical harmonic motion of frequency $\omega$, that the spreads stay saturated, and that the coherent energy law is the shifted Poisson law of parameter $|z|^{2}$ with spread $\hbar\omega|z|$. All of these are **conditional model deductions** from the adopted assumptions and the cited mathematics; they are not statements that any physical system is harmonic.

**What is empirical here.** Nothing on the page is a measured value. No numerical value of $m$, $\omega$ or $\hbar$ is asserted beyond the defining constants of the SI recorded in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], no spectral line or resonance is identified with an eigenvalue difference, and no laboratory preparation is identified with a coherent state. The quadratic potential is the leading approximation near a non-degenerate minimum of a smooth potential; the approximation's range, the deviations at finite amplitude and the transition to anharmonic behaviour are not derived here. The identification of the model's observables with apparatus readings is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]); agreement or disagreement of a laboratory oscillator with the model's predictions would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions and would not settle the framework's postulates.

## What is deferred

The Fourier-algebraic closure that this page consumes -- the diagonal operator, the Hermite family and its completeness, the scaling realization, the closed ladder domains and the coherent-vector convergence -- is authored on the mathematical page `qm-math-oscillator`; the one-dimensional non-normalizable formal solution of the ground-state equation and the ground-energy unit reading are authored on its examples companion `qm-math-oscillator-examples`, and this page links to them rather than duplicating them. The displacement-operator presentation of coherent states, overcompleteness and resolutions of unity, driven and damped oscillators, time-dependent parameters, anharmonic corrections, coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation and the identification of oscillator excitations with photons are separate model assumptions and are not developed here. Downstream pages that consume this page's items inherit the model scope stated in [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (e) and the conditional character of every derived claim.

## Status of the mathematics

The mathematical suppliers used here are the items of the run's mathematical oscillator page `qm-math-oscillator` and the published framework and spectral items cited in each item's contract; the two local lemmas [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-eigenspaces]] and [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] are proved on this page. Every proof item records its exact hypotheses, and no claim of this page is unconditional on the adopted postulates and model assumptions.
