items.title: The Gaussian ground state: position and momentum laws and the saturated bound
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\psi_0$ be the ground eigenvector of the model's energy operator $H_1$, let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, and let $Q$, $P$ be the model's position and momentum observables. Then:

(a) the class $\psi_0$ has the representative
$$\psi_0(x)=\ell^{-1/2}\pi^{-1/4}e^{-x^{2}/(2\ell^{2})},$$
it is a unit vector, it is the model's coherent state of label $0$, and $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$;

(b) the position outcome law of the assigned observable $(Q,\mathrm m)$ in the ground preparation has the density
$$f(x)=\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}},$$
with $\int_{\mathbb R}f=1$, mean $0$ and second moment $\ell^{2}/2$; hence $\Delta_{\psi_0}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$;

(c) the momentum outcome law of the assigned observable $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ has the density
$$g(p)=\frac{\ell}{\hbar\sqrt\pi}e^{-\ell^{2}p^{2}/\hbar^{2}},$$
with $\int_{\mathbb R}g=1$, mean $0$ and second moment $\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$; hence $\Delta_{\psi_0}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$;

(d) consequently $\Delta_{\psi_0}Q\,\Delta_{\psi_0}P=\hbar/2$: the ground preparation is one of the coherent preparations of [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-fluctuations]], and it saturates the model's position-momentum relation;

(e) the computation is one preparation of the adopted model; it identifies no measured distribution with $f$ or $g$ and no laboratory state with the ground state.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] with parameters $m,\omega,\hbar>0$, length $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, energy operator $H_1$, eigenbasis $(\psi_n)$ and ground vector $\psi_0$; the operators $Q$ and $P$ with their domains.

[F1] **The ground vector from the scaling theorem.** With $g_0(y)=\pi^{-1/4}e^{-y^{2}/2}$ and $D$ the scaling unitary of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]], one has $\psi_0=Dg_0$, $\psi_0(x)=\ell^{-1/2}g_0(x/\ell)=\ell^{-1/2}\pi^{-1/4}e^{-x^{2}/(2\ell^{2})}$, $\|\psi_0\|=1$, and $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$; moreover $\psi_0=\Psi_0$ is the coherent state of label $0$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b); [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] clause (a); [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]] clause (c); [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-energy-spectrum-and-completeness]] clause (a)).

[F2] **The position law.** $(Q,\mathrm m)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model with $Q=M_x$ on $D(Q)=\{f:xf\in L^{2}\}$ and law $\mu^{Q}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_Q(B)\psi\|^{2}$; for the real multiplier $m(x)=x$ on the $\sigma$-finite space $(\mathbb R,\text{Lebesgue})$ the assignment $E(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x^{-1}(B)}}$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $M_x$ and $\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{x^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}\,dx$ ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (b); [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b); [[lem-nrqm-observables-l2-multiplication-spectral-measure]] clauses (b), (c)).

[F3] **Heat kernel and its moments.** For $t>0$ and $n=1$, $\Gamma(x,t)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/(4t)}$ satisfies $\int\Gamma(x,t)dx=1$, and all first and second moments are absolutely integrable with $\int x\Gamma(x,t)dx=0$ and $\int x^{2}\Gamma(x,t)dx=2t$ ([[def-heat-kernel]], [[lem-heat-kernel-normalisation-scaling-and-derivatives]] clause (i), [[lem-first-and-second-moments-of-the-heat-kernel]]).

[F4] **The momentum law.** $\mathcal F_2(P\psi)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi\,\mathcal F_2\psi(\xi)$ for $\psi\in D(P)$, and $D(P)=\{\psi:\xi\mathcal F_2\psi\in L^{2}\}$; with $g(\xi):=2\pi\hbar\xi$ and $M_g$ the multiplication operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,d\xi)$ one has $P=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_g\mathcal F_2$ with $D(P)=\mathcal F_2^{-1}D(M_g)$, so by the transport lemma the spectral projection-valued measure of $P$ is $E_P(B)=\mathcal F_2^{-1}E_{M_g}(B)\mathcal F_2$ and, for a unit $\psi$, $\mu^{P}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{M_g}(B)\mathcal F_2\psi\|^{2}$; the multiplication lemma applied to $M_g$ gives $E_{M_g}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{g^{-1}(B)}}$ and $\mu^{P}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{g^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_2\psi(\xi)|^{2}\,d\xi$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (b) at $d=1$, $r=1$; [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (b), (c); [[lem-nrqm-observables-l2-multiplication-spectral-measure]] clauses (b), (c)).

[F5] **Gaussian Fourier transform and linear change of variables.** $\mathcal F_2(e^{-\pi tx^{2}})(\xi)=t^{-1/2}e^{-\pi\xi^{2}/t}$ for $t>0$ ([[lem-euclidean-gaussian-fourier-transform-with-two-pi-normalization]]); and for the $C^{1}$ diffeomorphism $T(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\xi$ of $\mathbb R$ and $h\in L^{1}$, $\int_{\mathbb R}h(p)\,dp=\int_{\mathbb R}h(2\pi\hbar\xi)\,2\pi\hbar\,d\xi$, so $\int_{\mathbb R}h(2\pi\hbar\xi)\,d\xi=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R}h(p)\,dp$ ([[cor-c-one-change-of-variables-for-l-one-functions]]).

[F6] **Means, variances and spreads.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ and a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the outcome-law mean and second moment exist and equal $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$, and the preparation spread is the square root of the outcome-law variance $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$; for the coherent preparations of the model the identity $\Delta Q\,\Delta P=\hbar/2$ is known ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b), (c); [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-fluctuations]] clause (a)).

## Verification

**Given:** the data of the Example and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [The ground vector] By [F1], $\psi_0=Dg_0$ with $g_0(y)=\pi^{-1/4}e^{-y^{2}/2}$, so its representative is $\psi_0(x)=\ell^{-1/2}\pi^{-1/4}e^{-x^{2}/(2\ell^{2})}$ and $\|\psi_0\|=\|g_0\|=1$ because $D$ is an isometry; $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$ and $\psi_0=\Psi_0$ are also from [F1]. [given, F1]

1.2 [The position law] By [F2] and [F1], for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the position law of the ground preparation is $\mu^{Q}_{\psi_0}(B)=\int_{x^{-1}(B)}|\psi_0(x)|^{2}dx=\int_B\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}}dx$, so $f(x)=\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}}$ is its density, with $\int f=1$ because $|\psi_0|^{2}$ is a probability density. [given, F1, F2]

1.3 [The momentum law] By [F4] and [F5], for every Borel $B$ the momentum law is $\mu^{P}_{\psi_0}(B)=\int_{g^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(\xi)|^{2}d\xi=\int_B(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(p/(2\pi\hbar))|^{2}dp$, using the substitution $p=2\pi\hbar\xi$ in the second step; hence the density is $g(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(p/(2\pi\hbar))|^{2}$. [given, F4, F5]

1.4 [The Fourier transform of the ground vector] By [F5] applied with $t=1/(2\pi\ell^{2})$, $\mathcal F_2(e^{-x^{2}/(2\ell^{2})})(\xi)=(\frac{1}{2\pi\ell^{2}})^{-1/2}e^{-2\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\ell\,e^{-2\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}$, so by [F1] $\mathcal F_2\psi_0(\xi)=\ell^{-1/2}\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt{2\pi}\,\ell\,e^{-2\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\ell^{1/2}\pi^{-1/4}e^{-2\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}$ and $|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(\xi)|^{2}=2\pi\ell\pi^{-1/2}e^{-4\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}=2\sqrt\pi\,\ell\,e^{-4\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}$. [given, F1, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (a)] By step 1.1 the ground vector has the displayed representative, is a unit vector, equals $\Psi_0$, and satisfies $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$. [step 1.1]

2.2 [Clause (b)] By step 1.2 the position density is $f(x)=\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}}$, which equals the heat kernel $\Gamma(x,\ell^{2}/4)$; by [F3] it integrates to $1$, and its mean and second moment are those of $\Gamma(\cdot,\ell^{2}/4)$: $\int x f=0$ and $\int x^{2}f=2\cdot\frac{\ell^{2}}{4}=\frac{\ell^{2}}{2}$. [step 1.2, F3]

2.3 [Clause (c)] By steps 1.3 and 1.4, $g(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}\cdot2\sqrt\pi\,\ell\,e^{-4\pi^{2}\ell^{2}(p/(2\pi\hbar))^{2}}=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}2\sqrt\pi\,\ell\,e^{-\ell^{2}p^{2}/\hbar^{2}}=\frac{\ell}{\hbar\sqrt\pi}e^{-\ell^{2}p^{2}/\hbar^{2}}$, which equals the heat kernel $\Gamma(p,\hbar^{2}/(4\ell^{2}))$; by [F3] it integrates to $1$ and has mean $0$ and second moment $2\cdot\frac{\hbar^{2}}{4\ell^{2}}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}$. [step 1.3, step 1.4, F3]

3.1 [Clause (d)] By steps 2.2 and 2.3 the ground preparation has position variance $\ell^{2}/2$ and momentum variance $\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$, so by [F6] its spreads are $\Delta_{\psi_0}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$ and $\Delta_{\psi_0}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ with product $\hbar/2$; by [F6] this is the value of the coherent preparations, and by [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-fluctuations]] it is the minimum of the spread product over the common domain. [step 2.2, step 2.3, F6]

4.1 [Clause (e)] The computation used only the model's ground vector, the multiplication and Fourier forms of the model's position and momentum observables and the Gaussian heat-kernel facts; no measured distribution, apparatus or empirical value entered. [step 3.1, given] ∎

items.title: Ladder norms and excitation statistics of the oscillator eigenstates
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(\psi_n)$ be the model's complete orthonormal eigenbasis, $a_\psi,a^\dagger_\psi,N_\psi$ the transported ladder and number operators of [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-energy-spectrum-and-completeness]] clause (b), and $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$. Then:

(a) the first ladder images and their norms are
$$a_\psi\psi_0=0,\quad a_\psi\psi_1=\psi_0,\quad a_\psi\psi_2=\sqrt2\,\psi_1,\qquad a^\dagger_\psi\psi_0=\psi_1,\quad a^\dagger_\psi\psi_1=\sqrt2\,\psi_2,$$
$$\|a_\psi\psi_1\|=1,\quad\|a_\psi\psi_2\|=\sqrt2,\quad\|a^\dagger_\psi\psi_0\|=1,\quad\|a^\dagger_\psi\psi_1\|=\sqrt2;$$

(b) the matrix elements of the ladder operators in the eigenbasis are
$$\langle\psi_m,a_\psi\psi_n\rangle=\sqrt n\,\delta_{m,n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad\langle\psi_m,a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}\,\delta_{m,n+1},\qquad\langle a_\psi\psi_n,a_\psi\psi_m\rangle=n\,\delta_{nm};$$

(c) every eigenvector is an eigenvector of the number operator, $N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n$, and the number and energy outcome laws of the eigenstate preparations are the point masses
$$\mu^{N_\psi}_{\psi_n}(\{n\})=1,\qquad \mu^{H_1}_{\psi_n}\bigl(\{E_n\}\bigr)=1:$$
the $n$-th eigenstate preparation carries exactly $n$ excitations and the energy $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$;

(d) the annihilation and creation operators are not assigned sharp observables of the model: they are not self-adjoint, so their images and norms are operator-theoretic quantities, not outcome values; the assigned sharp observables of the model are $(Q,\mathrm m)$, $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$, $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and $N_\psi$ (with the counting unit), and only laws of those are read in clause (c);

(e) the computation is a finite low-level check of the ladder relations in the adopted model, not a measurement record and not a claim that a laboratory oscillator was prepared in an eigenstate.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the one-dimensional oscillator model with parameters $m,\omega,\hbar>0$; its complete orthonormal eigenbasis $(\psi_n)$ with $H_1\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$ and $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$; the closed ladder and number operators $a_\psi,a^\dagger_\psi,N_\psi$ of the model's spectrum theorem clause (b).

[F1] **Eigenbasis and ladder operators.** $(\psi_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family of $H_1$, $H_1\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$, $N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n$, and on the eigenbasis $a_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$ with $a_\psi\psi_0=0$, $a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}$ and $a^\dagger_\psi a_\psi=N_\psi$, $a_\psi a^\dagger_\psi=N_\psi+I$ on the common domain; the operators $a_\psi$, $a^\dagger_\psi$ are closed, $a_\psi^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$, and $N_\psi$ is self-adjoint with eigenbasis $(\psi_n)$; the number law of $N_\psi$ in the pure preparation of $\psi_n$ is $\delta_n$, and the energy law of $H_1$ is the atomic law $\mu^{H_1}_{\psi_n}(\{E_n\})=|\langle\psi_n,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}=1$ ([[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-energy-spectrum-and-completeness]] clauses (a), (b), (c); [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] clauses (b), (d), (e); [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F2] **Assigned observables and their laws.** The model assigns the status of assigned sharp observable to $(Q,\mathrm m)$, $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$, $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and, through the number operator, to the excitation number; their outcome laws are read from the spectral measures, and an operator that is not self-adjoint is not an assigned sharp observable of the framework ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (b), (c); [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]).

[F3] **Orthonormality.** $\langle\psi_n,\psi_m\rangle=\delta_{nm}$ and $\|\psi_n\|=1$ for every $n$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (a)).

## Verification

**Given:** the data of the Example and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Ladder images] By [F1], $a_\psi\psi_0=0$, $a_\psi\psi_1=\sqrt1\psi_0=\psi_0$, $a_\psi\psi_2=\sqrt2\psi_1$, $a^\dagger_\psi\psi_0=\sqrt1\psi_1=\psi_1$ and $a^\dagger_\psi\psi_1=\sqrt2\psi_2$. [given, F1]

1.2 [Matrix elements] By [F1] and [F3], for $n\ge1$ and every $m$, $\langle\psi_m,a_\psi\psi_n\rangle=\sqrt n\langle\psi_m,\psi_{n-1}\rangle=\sqrt n\,\delta_{m,n-1}$, $\langle\psi_m,a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}\langle\psi_m,\psi_{n+1}\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}\,\delta_{m,n+1}$, and $\langle a_\psi\psi_n,a_\psi\psi_m\rangle=\sqrt{nm}\langle\psi_{n-1},\psi_{m-1}\rangle=n\,\delta_{nm}$ for $n,m\ge1$. [given, F1, F3]

1.3 [Number and energy laws of the eigenstates] By [F1], $N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n$ and the number law of the unit eigenvector $\psi_n$ is $\delta_n$; likewise the energy law of the unit eigenvector is $\mu^{H_1}_{\psi_n}(\{E_n\})=|\langle\psi_n,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}=1$ by [F1] and [F3], so the preparation carries exactly $n$ excitations and the energy value $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$. [given, F1, F3]

2.1 [Clause (a)] Taking norms in the images of step 1.1 and using $\|\psi_k\|=1$ of [F3] gives $\|a_\psi\psi_1\|=\|\psi_0\|=1$, $\|a_\psi\psi_2\|=\sqrt2\|\psi_1\|=\sqrt2$, $\|a^\dagger_\psi\psi_0\|=\|\psi_1\|=1$ and $\|a^\dagger_\psi\psi_1\|=\sqrt2\|\psi_2\|=\sqrt2$. [step 1.1, F3]

2.2 [Clause (b)] The displays of clause (b) are exactly the identities computed in step 1.2. [step 1.2]

3.1 [Clause (d)] By [F2] the assigned sharp observables are the self-adjoint ones listed; $a_\psi$ and $a^\dagger_\psi$ are not self-adjoint by [F1], so the norms computed in clauses (a) and (b) are norms of operator images and not outcome values of any assigned sharp observable of the model. [step 1.3, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F2]

4.1 [Clause (e)] The computation used the model's eigenbasis and ladder operators and the orthonormality of the eigenbasis; it produced no measurement record and no claim about a laboratory preparation. [step 1.3, step 3.1, given] ∎

items.title: A coherent-state trajectory: period, phase-space ellipse and constant spreads
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix a label $z=z_1+iz_2$ with $|z|>0$, let $x_0:=\sqrt2\,\ell z_1$, $p_0:=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}z_2$, let $\Psi_z(t):=U(t)\Psi_z$ be the evolved coherent state, and write $x(t):=\langle Q\Psi_z(t),\Psi_z(t)\rangle$, $p(t):=\langle P\Psi_z(t),\Psi_z(t)\rangle$. Then:

(a) the preparation is periodic with period $\frac{2\pi}{\omega}$ in the sense that the prepared state is the same pure preparation at times $t$ and $t+\frac{2\pi}{\omega}$:
$$[U(2\pi/\omega)\Psi_z]=[\Psi_z],\qquad [\Psi_z(t+2\pi/\omega)]=[\Psi_z(t)]\quad(t\in\mathbb R);$$

(b) the mean pair is
$$x(t)=x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t,\qquad p(t)=p_0\cos\omega t-m\omega x_0\sin\omega t,$$
so that $x(0)=x_0$, $p(0)=p_0$, and at the quarter period $x\bigl(\frac{\pi}{2\omega}\bigr)=\frac{p_0}{m\omega}$, $p\bigl(\frac{\pi}{2\omega}\bigr)=-m\omega x_0$; the phase-space ellipse
$$\frac{x(t)^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}+\frac{\ell^{2}p(t)^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=|z|^{2}$$
is invariant along the motion;

(c) the position and momentum spreads and their product are constant along the motion:
$$\Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}P=\frac{\hbar}{2}\quad(t\in\mathbb R);$$

(d) the displayed $x(t)$ and $p(t)$ are preparation means of the model's position and momentum observables in the evolving coherent preparation; they are not the coordinates of a measured particle trajectory, and no measurement record, apparatus or empirical value is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the one-dimensional oscillator model with parameters $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and length $\ell$; the coherent states $\Psi_z$ and their evolution $\Psi_z(t)=U(t)\Psi_z$; the label $z=z_1+iz_2\ne0$ and the numbers $x_0=\sqrt2\ell z_1$, $p_0=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}z_2$; a real time $t$.

[F1] **Coherent evolution and its statistics.** For every $w\in\mathbb C$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, $U(s)\Psi_w=e^{-i\omega s/2}\Psi_{we^{-i\omega s}}$; the preparation means of the evolved coherent preparation are $\langle Q\rangle_{w(s)}=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}w(s)$, $\langle P\rangle_{w(s)}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}w(s)$ with $w(s)=we^{-i\omega s}$; and $\Delta_{\Psi_{w(s)}}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$, $\Delta_{\Psi_{w(s)}}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ with product $\hbar/2$ ([[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-evolution]] clauses (a), (b), (c); [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-fluctuations]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F2] **Trigonometric identities.** For real $\theta$, $e^{-i\theta}=\cos\theta-i\sin\theta$, $\cos^{2}\theta+\sin^{2}\theta=1$, $\cos 0=\sin\pi/2$ properties in the form $\cos 0=1$, $\sin 0=0$, $\cos\frac{\pi}{2}=0$, $\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=1$, and $e^{-2\pi i}=1$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]).

[F3] **Spread reading.** The preparation spreads in [F1] are the outcome-law spreads of the assigned observables $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b), (c), and the means are the outcome-law means of [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-evolution]] clause (b).

## Verification

**Given:** the data of the Example and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [The evolved family] By [F1] applied with $w=z$ and $s=t$, $\Psi_z(t)=U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ with $z(t)=ze^{-i\omega t}$, and the means and spreads of the evolved preparation are those of the coherent label $z(t)$. [given, F1]

1.2 [The complex label in real form] By [F2], $e^{-i\omega t}=\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t$, so $z(t)=z(\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t)$ has real part $z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t$ and imaginary part $z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t$, and $\cos^{2}\omega t+\sin^{2}\omega t=1$; also $e^{-2\pi i}=1$. [given, F2]

2.1 [Clause (a)] By step 1.1 and [F2], $z(t+2\pi/\omega)=ze^{-i\omega t}e^{-2\pi i}=z(t)$ and $e^{-i\omega(t+2\pi/\omega)/2}=e^{-i\omega t/2}e^{-i\pi}=-e^{-i\omega t/2}$, so $U(2\pi/\omega)\Psi_z=-\Psi_z$; a global phase does not change the pure preparation, hence $[U(2\pi/\omega)\Psi_z]=[\Psi_z]$ and $[\Psi_z(t+2\pi/\omega)]=[\Psi_z(t)]$ for every $t$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F2]

2.2 [Clause (b)] By step 1.1 and [F1], $x(t)=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t)$ and $p(t)=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t)$; substituting the real and imaginary parts of step 1.2 and using $x_0=\sqrt2\ell z_1$, $\frac{p_0}{m\omega}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_2}{\ell m\omega}=\sqrt2\ell z_2$, $m\omega x_0=\sqrt2 m\omega\ell z_1=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_1}{\ell}$ by $\ell^{2}=\hbar/(m\omega)$ gives the two displayed closed forms; at $t=0$ they read $x_0,p_0$, and at $t=\frac{\pi}{2\omega}$ they read $\frac{p_0}{m\omega}$ and $-m\omega x_0$ by the values in [F2]. For the ellipse, the closed forms give $\frac{x(t)^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}=(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)^{2}$ and $\frac{\ell^{2}p(t)^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)^{2}$; adding, the cross terms cancel and $\cos^{2}\omega t+\sin^{2}\omega t=1$ gives the sum $z_1^{2}+z_2^{2}=|z|^{2}$ for every $t$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F2, algebra]

2.3 [Clause (c)] By step 1.1 the evolved preparation is the coherent preparation of label $z(t)$, so [F1] gives $\Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$, $\Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ and product $\hbar/2$ for every $t$. [step 1.1, F1]

3.1 [Clause (d)] By [F3] the quantities $x(t)$, $p(t)$ are outcome-law means of the model's position and momentum observables in the evolving preparation, and the spreads are outcome-law spreads; no measurement record, apparatus model or empirical value entered the computation. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, F3] ∎

items.title: What the worked oscillator examples establish
items.statement:
## What the worked items establish

**Ground state.** [[ex-nrqm-oscillator-ground-state-gaussian]] fixes the explicit Gaussian representative $\psi_0(x)=\ell^{-1/2}\pi^{-1/4}e^{-x^{2}/(2\ell^{2})}$ of the ground vector, its unit norm, the eigenvalue equation $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$, the position law with density $\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}}$ and variance $\ell^{2}/2$, the momentum law with density $\frac{\ell}{\hbar\sqrt\pi}e^{-\ell^{2}p^{2}/\hbar^{2}}$ and variance $\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$, and the saturation $\Delta_{\psi_0}Q\,\Delta_{\psi_0}P=\hbar/2$ of the model's position-momentum relation.

**Ladder and excitation structure.** [[ex-nrqm-oscillator-ladder-norms]] computes the first ladder images and their norms, the ladder matrix elements $\langle\psi_m,a_\psi\psi_n\rangle=\sqrt n\,\delta_{m,n-1}$ and $\langle\psi_m,a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}\,\delta_{m,n+1}$, and the excitation and energy laws $\mu^{N_\psi}_{\psi_n}(\{n\})=1$, $\mu^{H_1}_{\psi_n}(\{E_n\})=1$ of the eigenstate preparations, with the warning that $a_\psi$ and $a^\dagger_\psi$ are not assigned sharp observables.

**Coherent motion.** [[ex-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-trajectory]] shows that a nonzero-label coherent preparation is periodic with period $2\pi/\omega$, that its mean pair traces the invariant phase-space ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}+\frac{\ell^{2}p^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=|z|^{2}$ with the quarter-period values $x(\frac{\pi}{2\omega})=\frac{p_0}{m\omega}$, $p(\frac{\pi}{2\omega})=-m\omega x_0$, and that the position and momentum spreads and their product $\hbar/2$ are constant along the motion.

## What they do not establish

Every computation above is conditional on the adopted oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] and on the postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5 read through it; none of them reports a measurement. In particular: no numerical value of $m$, $\omega$ or $\hbar$ is extracted; no laboratory state is identified with $\psi_0$, with an eigenstate $\psi_n$ or with a coherent state; the mean functions $x(t),p(t)$ are preparation means of the model's observables under the evolving preparation and are not the coordinates of a measured trajectory; and the periodicity of clause (a) of the coherent-trajectory example is a statement about the pure preparation (a ray), not about a measured signal. The harmonic approximation's range, anharmonic corrections, damping, driving, time-dependent parameters and coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation are outside the examples, as is the displacement-operator presentation of the coherent family. The one-dimensional non-normalizable formal solution of the ground-state equation is authored on the mathematical companion `qm-math-oscillator-examples` and is linked there, not duplicated here.
